A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 18-page work, including Appendices A–I. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to running headers and first-page version/date markings.

before.justification: v4 reports original EEG/MEG generation experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, and caption-quality analyses in Section 4 and Appendices H–I.

after.justification: v5 reports the same original EEG/MEG generation results, baseline comparisons, ablations, and caption-quality analyses in Section 4 and Appendices H–I.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A–C retain identical DiT/DDIM procedures, CLIP image/text conditioning, cross-attention, spatio-temporal embeddings, training objective, and inference algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image-conditioned brain-signal generation on THINGS-EEG2 and THINGS-MEG, with identical participant coverage, within-subject and cross-subject scenarios, and caption-quality evaluations.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Güçlü and Van Gerven, Yamins et al., and SynBrain as baselines. Tables 5–6 retain VisualGLM and MiniGPT-4 as alternative caption generators; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices D–F report identical splits, preprocessing, subject-transfer procedures, sample sizes, evaluation metrics, and model/training settings. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The component ablations, brain-region ablations, cross-subject topographies, and caption-quality analyses are identical in Section 4 and Appendices H–I.

E5.justification: Subject-averaging statements and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All table entries and plotted results match, including appendix caption distributions. For example, Tables 1–2 retain within-subject MSE/Pearson values of 0.109/0.425 for EEG and 0.663/0.379 for MEG.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations in Section 3 and Appendices A–C are identical, including the diffusion equations, embedding definitions, and loss. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about biologically plausible M/EEG generation, the proposed architectural components, benchmark superiority, and relevance to visual prostheses.

C2.justification: Both versions give the same interpretations of cross-subject degradation, occipital-region importance, and caption quality. The discussion of inter-individual variability and future research is unchanged, with no new limitations or applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendices B–G retain identical channel grouping, padding, preprocessing, pseudocode, architecture, optimizer, batch sizes, and hardware disclosures. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, the baseline positioning in Appendix G, and the bibliography are unchanged. No cited works or substantive relationships to prior research are added, removed, or revised.

P1.justification: v5 replaces the running header 'Submission and Formatting Instructions for ICML 2026' on pages 2–18 with the paper title. It also updates the preprint date and arXiv version/date markings; body prose and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–8, captions, axes, legends, sizing, and placement are unchanged. The running-header wording changes within the existing header layout, without reflowing the document.

improvement.justification: v5 replaces the misleading ICML template running header with the actual paper title throughout the main text and appendices. This corrects a visible editorial defect and modestly improves document identification and polish. Scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged.
